source: windows-console-driver estate window 19 (GPME on Windows Server 2025, capability gpmc.observe_imported_firewall_rules revision 1, record docs/estate-window-19/records/w19-r3-record.json, 2026-10-20, state verified). Plan 035 WP-2, WI-077.
what_was_imported: studio-firewall-backup.zip built at gpo-studio badcaf9 by scripts/plan-033/build-firewall-candidate.py (sha256 3f146885bb8e362e4d178582cc5710cd8067980cb9413a5411c75e2edf651e0f, the same bytes the 1.1.0 batch's firewall lane imported), Import-GPO into a disposable unlinked GPO. The record's pre-state gPCMachineExtensionNames equals [{35378EAC-683F-11D2-A89A-00C04FBBCFA2}{B05566AC-FE9C-4368-BE01-7A4CBB6CBA11}], the export's firewall-only registration (WI-075). The D02B1F72 registration that WI-077 originally asked about was not observed: badcaf9 no longer writes it for a firewall-only GPO.
oracle: State half: the w19-r3 envelope, post == pre on both version halves, versionNumber, both extension lists and the imported Registry.pol (PSDirect SYSVOL + AD reads, controller-side). GPME's browse also wrote SYSVOL: a GptTmpl.inf stub with its SecEdit parents and the Machine/Scripts/{Startup,Shutdown} directories; revision 1 did not pin that delta exactly, revision 2 (record_binding) does. Display half: NOT an oracle. It is GPME's own Inbound Rules list as the UIA tree exposes it, kept for a person to review beside the screenshots.

inbound-rules.json.derivation: The results list's 18 HeaderItem names become columns. Each ListItem (the rule name), its in-place Edit twin and the following 17 Text cells become one row, in GPME's display order (sorted by Name, the disabled rule last). Values are verbatim.

companion_evidence: windows-console-driver docs/estate-window-19/captures/: wp2-firewall-overview.{png,uia.json}, wp2-inbound-rules.png, wp2-rule-properties.{png,uia.json} (StudioFwLane in tcp allow Properties: General tab, nine tabs, Enabled ticked, Allow selected, Apply greyed), wp2-after-cancel.png.
limitations: Display and controls only. No edit was made, so nothing shows that an edit through GPME persists to Registry.pol. UIA exposes no enabled/disabled state for the sheet's controls, so editability is read off the screenshot by a person. One build, one estate, one run.
sanitisation: Synthetic StudioFwLane rule names and group, RFC 5737/3849 documentation addresses (198.51.100.7, 192.0.2.0/24, 2001:db8::/32), synthetic ports 65001-65007. No domain, host, account or SID values.
record_binding: Revision 2 (windows-console-driver estate window 20, docs/estate-window-20/records/w20-r2-record.json, verified) re-ran the observation with the input and evidence bound by the record: its notes carry bundle_sha256=3f146885bb8e362e4d178582cc5710cd8067980cb9413a5411c75e2edf651e0f, backup_id=cb31b508-35ee-54e1-9dad-fb54db071b99 and the imported registry_pol_sha256=25ad9748d1872472abcc7b8992016989c011e9b60fda3fc5dfc53e8b179de081; its journal binds the saved UIA dumps by SHA-256; and its envelope pins the exact SYSVOL delta (a 142-byte GptTmpl.inf stub, sha256 07cba636ed9c1c30c4a4c228e555151f1fc43f7bfc941cbb221ed67297ea3dbc, absent before; its SecEdit parents; Machine/Scripts/{Startup,Shutdown}). Its inbound-rule text cells are identical to the window-19 capture this fixture was derived from. Revision 3 (estate window 21, docs/estate-window-21/records/w21-r2-record.json, verified) re-observed the same exact delta with the GptTmpl.inf parse asserted leaf by leaf, and its untruncated provenance.invocation carries gpo_stage_import's whole output (backup id, bundle hash, imported Registry.pol hash). SUPERSEDED/CURRENT (2026-10-21): w21-r2 is banked as superseded (record-schema v2 with a retrofitted field). The current evidence is revision 4, docs/estate-window-22/records/w22-r2-record.json (record-schema v3, verified), whose invocation carries gpo_stage_import's whole output and whose bundle digest and expectations are pinned to the banked values.
